message.content:
**Hydrogen – A Quick Reference to Its Key Properties**

| Category | Property | Value / Description |
|----------|----------|---------------------|
| **Basic Atomic Data** | Atomic number | 1 |
| | Atomic mass (average) | 1.008 u |
| | Electron configuration | 1s¹ |
| | Isotopes | ¹H (protium, 99.98 %), ²H (deuterium, 0.02 %), ³H (tritium, trace) |
| | Electronegativity (Pauling) | 2.20 |
| | First ionization energy | 13.598 eV (1312 kJ mol⁻¹) |
| | Electron affinity | –0.754 eV (–72.8 kJ mol⁻¹) |
| **Physical State (25 °C, 1 atm)** | State | Gas |
| | Boiling point | –252.87 °C (20.28 K) |
| | Melting point | –259.16 °C (14.01 K) |
| | Density | 0.08988 g L⁻¹ |
| | Molar volume | 22.414 L mol⁻¹ |
| | Specific heat (gas, 1 bar) | 28.836 J mol⁻¹ K⁻¹ |
| | Thermal conductivity | 0.180 W m⁻¹ K⁻¹ |
| | Speed of sound | ~ 1270 m s⁻¹ (at 20 °C) |
| **Chemical Properties** | Oxidation states | +1 (most common), –1 (hydride) |
| | Common compounds | H₂O, H₂SO₄, HCl, NH₃, CH₄, etc. |
| | Bonding | Forms covalent bonds (H–H single bond), ionic bonds as hydride (H⁻), and participates in hydrogen bonding (e.g., in water). |
| | Reactivity | Highly flammable; reacts with oxygen to form water (exothermic). Forms hydrides with metals (e.g., NaH). |
| | Acid–base behavior | Acts as a weak acid (e.g., HCl) or base (e.g., NH₃). |
| | Redox behavior | Can be oxidized to water or reduced to metal hydrides. |
| **Isotopic Variants** | Deuterium (²H) | Heavier isotope; used in nuclear fusion research, as a tracer in chemistry, and in heavy water (D₂O). |
| | Tritium (³H) | Radioactive; used in nuclear fusion experiments and as a tracer in biology. |
| **Physical & Chemical Uses** | Fuel | Hydrogen gas is a clean fuel (produces only water when combusted). |
| | Industry | Used in ammonia synthesis (Haber process), petroleum refining, metal hydride batteries, and as a reducing agent. |
| | Space & Energy | Potential fuel for rockets (liquid hydrogen + liquid oxygen). |
| | Research | Studied in quantum mechanics, astrophysics (stellar fusion), and materials science. |
| **Astrophysical Role** | Stellar fusion | Hydrogen nuclei fuse to form helium in stars (proton–proton chain, CNO cycle). |
| | Big Bang nucleosynthesis | Produced ~75 % of the universe’s baryonic mass. |
| | Interstellar medium | Exists as H I (neutral), H₂ (molecular), and ionized H II regions. |
| **Safety & Handling** | Flammability | Extremely flammable; explosive limits 4–75 % in air. |
| | Toxicity | Non‑toxic, but can cause asphyxiation in confined spaces due to displacement of oxygen. |
| | Storage | Requires high‑pressure cylinders or cryogenic tanks (liquid hydrogen). |
| **Miscellaneous** | Spectral lines | Lyman series (UV), Balmer series (visible), Paschen series (IR). |
| | Quantum properties | Exhibits wave–particle duality; ground state is a singlet. |
| | Standard state | Defined at 0 °C, 1 atm; used as a reference for thermodynamic tables. |

---

### Quick Takeaways

- **Lightest element**: Hydrogen is the simplest atom, with one proton and one electron.
- **Highly reactive**: Forms a wide variety of compounds, from water to hydrocarbons.
- **Key in energy**: Central to both fossil‑fuel chemistry and future clean‑energy technologies (fuel cells, hydrogen‑powered vehicles, rocket propellants).
- **Astrophysical cornerstone**: The fuel of stars and the most abundant element in the universe.
- **Isotopic diversity**: Deuterium and tritium give hydrogen unique roles in nuclear fusion and scientific tracing.

Feel free to ask for deeper dives into any of these aspects—whether it’s the quantum mechanics of the H₂ molecule, the thermodynamics of hydrogen storage, or the role of hydrogen in planetary atmospheres!
